summary.text: This opportunity briefing explores combining RAG, cross-modal retrieval, and natural language queries to improve report generation and analysis tasks in volumetric medical imaging, such as assessing inflammatory bowel disease through CT enterography. The integration of cross-modal retrieval driven by natural language queries within a retrieval-augmented generation framework helps models leverage relevant retrieved context to improve severity accuracy and ordinal error rates. This approach addresses the limitation where fine-tuning language models for report generation without external retrieval context yields limited ordering beyond the baseline class distribution and results in poor severity accuracy.

target_user.text: The target user is unverified based on the patent assignee categories, but repositories in the bundle indicate applications in healthcare data benchmarking and medical multimodal contrastive learning.

jtbd.text: Generate accurate medical reports and perform volumetric medical image analysis by retrieving relevant multi-source items across heterogeneous modalities using natural language query interfaces.

value_prop.text: Leverages relevant retrieved context to improve severity accuracy and ordinal error rates in medical report generation compared to fine-tuning language models without external retrieval context.

riskiest_assumption.text: The riskiest assumption is designated as axis V (viability) due to missing evidence. We assume that healthcare organizations are willing to pay for and adopt a RAG-based volumetric medical imaging analysis platform.

mvp.text: Conduct customer interviews and a price acceptance test with potential medical imaging users, presenting mockup workflows and proposed pricing to test the viability assumption.
mvp.type: customer interviews and price acceptance test

success_metric.text: Achieve a proposed threshold of 40 percent positive willingness-to-pay responses during customer interviews and price acceptance testing, as motivated by DVF viability axis evaluation (dvf:14).

kill_criteria.text: Kill the project if fewer than a proposed threshold of 15 percent of interviewed healthcare stakeholders express willingness to adopt or pay for the tool, as motivated by DVF viability axis evaluation (dvf:14).

open_source.use: Serves as a multimodal benchmark for healthcare data to evaluate different multimodal retrieval tasks.
Provides code for improving medical multi-modal contrastive learning with expert annotations.

to_build.text: Develop a volumetric medical image preprocessing module with multi-window RGB encoding for CT enterography data ingestion, motivated by findings in paper:2604.13021.
